findings.location: Paragraph 2 — sentence: “Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups.
findings.source_quote: “Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the meaning clearly: translate “smart” as a cognitive judgment (e.g., ‘slim’ or ‘dom’ depending on tone) and translate “Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups” idiomatically so the resignation is clear. For example: “’Jamin, jy sal nooit slim wees nie,” het Kenny gesê. Diep binne-in het Jamin hom by ’n lewe van verwarde struikelings bepas gevoel.” (Or better: “Diep binne-in het Jamin hom by ’n lewe van onsekerheid en konstante foutjies neergeleë gevoel.”)
findings.translation_quote: “Jamin, jy sal nooit slim wees nie,” het Kenny gesê. Tief binne-in het Jamin hom by ’n lewe van verwarde struikelings gevoeg gevoel.

findings.location: Paragraph 3 — sentence: “Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart.”
findings.source_quote: Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart.
findings.suggested_fix: ‘Simple’ here means ‘not intelligent’ (pejorative), not ‘simple’ in the neutral sense. Translate to a clear Afrikaans equivalent that carries the intended meaning (e.g., ‘dom’). Example: “Goed dan — Jamin sal dom wees. Kenny sal slim wees.”
findings.translation_quote: Goed dan, Jamin sal eenvoudig wees. Kenny sal slim wees.

findings.source_quote: A narrow path winding through a leafy woodland
findings.suggested_fix: Alt text should match the original. Replace inaccurate adjective ‘slyperige’ (slippery) with a neutral descriptor for ‘narrow’, e.g., ‘’n nou paadjie wat deur ’n blarevolle woud kronkel’ or keep the translator’s ‘kronkel’ but change ‘slyperige’ to ‘nou’.
findings.translation_quote: ’n Slyperige paadjie wat deur ’n blarevolle woud kronkel

findings.location: Paragraph describing light through trees — “his golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees.”
findings.source_quote: his golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees.
findings.suggested_fix: The translation uses inappropriate verb choices that obscure the image (“geknou”, “wegflikker” earlier). Use clearer, idiomatic Afrikaans to preserve the pastoral image. Example: “Sy goue kop het die moeg strale opgevang wat, terwyl hulle tussen die bome flikker, van die son wegkruip.”
findings.translation_quote: Sy goue kop het die moeg strale geknou wat van die son wegflikker deur die bome.

findings.location: Paragraph where darkness stains the ground — “Darkness stained the ground around Kenny.”
findings.source_quote: Darkness stained the ground around Kenny.
findings.suggested_fix: ‘Stained the ground’ is rendered oddly as ‘aangeteken’. Use a verb that conveys the sense of darkness settling or spreading, e.g., ‘’n donker vlek het die grond rondom Kenny geteken’ or ‘donkerheid het die grond rondom Kenny oorval’.
findings.translation_quote: Duisternis het die grond om Kenny aangeteken.
